doc: The sources a project report can read, as DATA: what a connection to each asks for, what its scope may name, the read-only permissions a token needs (with the official pages they were checked against), the published token shapes a log must never show, and which permission each optional part of the report depends on. One project uses exactly ONE of these.

fields.name: host
fields.label: API host
fields.doc: https://api.github.com, or https://<your-server>/api/v3 for GitHub Enterprise Server

fields.name: organization
fields.label: Owner (organization or user)
fields.doc: The account that owns the repositories. A fine-grained token reaches one owner.

fields.name: repositories
fields.label: Repositories
fields.doc: owner/name, one or more, all under this connection's owner

fields.name: projects
fields.label: Projects (v2) numbers
fields.doc: Optional: organization project numbers whose Status and Iteration fields the report may map

strategies.label: Personal access token or environment variable
strategies.doc: A fine-grained personal access token, stored once in this machine's secret store, or the name of an environment variable that holds it.

credential.advice: Create a fine-grained personal access token for the owner above, limited to the repositories this report reads, with READ-ONLY repository permissions: Metadata, Pull requests, Issues — and Actions and Deployments if those parts are on. Add the organization permission Projects (read) only if Projects are read. Never grant a write permission for a report.

fields.name: host
fields.label: Organization URL
fields.doc: https://dev.azure.com for Azure DevOps Services, or your Azure DevOps Server collection URL

fields.name: organization
fields.label: Organization
fields.doc: The organization (Services) — a token is scoped to exactly one

fields.name: project
fields.label: Project
fields.doc: The project whose Boards, Repos and Pipelines are read
fields.says: the project's NAME as Azure DevOps shows it, not its URL -- it cannot contain \ / : * ? " < > | # % &

fields.name: repositories
fields.label: Repositories
fields.doc: Repository names; empty reads every repository of the project

fields.name: team
fields.label: Team
fields.doc: Whose iterations define the periods; empty uses the project's default team

fields.name: areaPath
fields.label: Area path
fields.doc: Optional: only work items under this area path

strategies.label: Microsoft sign-in
strategies.doc: Sign in once with a Microsoft account. Orbit then asks for a short-lived Azure DevOps access token each time it needs one -- the token is never stored -- and signs in again only when the session itself ends. Orbit signs in through an Azure CLI profile of its own: it never uses, reads or changes the account you may be signed in with in your own terminal, so the two can even be different accounts.

options.name: tenant
options.label: Directory (tenant)
options.doc: The Microsoft Entra directory that owns this organization, as its id or domain. Only needed when your account belongs to more than one directory.

options.name: deviceCode
options.label: Use a device code
options.doc: Sign in with a code you enter on another device, for a machine with no browser or a policy that blocks the browser sign-in.

strategies.label: Personal access token or environment variable
strategies.doc: A personal access token, stored once in this machine's secret store, or the name of an environment variable that holds it. Use it when Microsoft sign-in is not possible here.

credential.advice: Only needed when this connection uses a token instead of Microsoft sign-in. Create a personal access token scoped to this ONE organization (global tokens stop working on 1 December 2026) with READ scopes only: Work Items (Read), Code (Read), Build (Read), Project and Team (Read) — and Release (Read) if classic releases are read. Never grant Read & write for a report.
